result.summary:
PR 208 (CORNERFACE2, qwen) should not be merged. The brief's own red test is still red on the branch: the dispatcher's run gave CORNER_FACE failures=208 checks=1082, and the seat's own run gave 274. That count changes between runs, so the ruler is not stable either. The fix itself (brief step 4) is missing: CornerShots.frame is unchanged for ots and cutman. The only game change moves code into a new CornerShots.lens(), and that move breaks things. It ignores the drift: `_u` is unused and the look is computed from the undrifted fr.pos while the camera films the drifted p, so a drifting shot with the card up slides the face off its spot. It also changes what reverse and other aim at.

The ruler breaks the brief's core rules. It reads the BODY's forward as the face direction (corner_face_scene.gd:50, which the brief forbids), so the head-turn check and check (c) are measured wrongly. The seat admits this as a 'known issue'. Every seed rebuilds the whole crew with crew.build(), which leaves the crew unplaced for seeds 1-9 and attaches extra CornerIK nodes. It projects points by hand instead of using the camera's unproject_position. The mutants go through a separate copy of the check code, and that copy has no (c) check at all. The mirror check cannot fail, because the blue coach is placed from the red coach's measured offsets. The table is a header with nothing under it. Step 3 (red on main, committed alone), step 5 (three runs) and step 6 (stills) were not done. E:/FightCamp/tmp/cornerface2 does not exist, so there was no still or film frame to open.

Merging against main: none of the five files has changed on main since the merge base 1e336b04, so the diff would apply cleanly. REST1 (6fa2b52b, Attrs/rest) does not touch these files. A clean apply does not change the verdict. Re-brief CORNERFACE2 using the problem list below.

problems.issue: The face direction is the body's forward (skel basis * BACK). The brief forbids this, and it makes the head-turn check, check (c), the ears and the nose all wrong.
problems.fix: Inside _capture: var h := skel.find_bone("Head"); var ik: Object = skel.get_node_or_null("CornerIK"); face_dirs[skel] = (skel.global_transform.basis * (skel.get_bone_global_pose(h).basis.orthonormalized() * ik._face_local)).normalized()

problems.issue: apply_seed calls crew.build(stage, true) every seed: it loads a new set of crew bodies (old ones leaked and still visible), attaches more CornerIK nodes to the boxers, and leaves seeds 1-9 filming a crew no cue placed.

problems.issue: lens() ignores u and the drift; the look is aimed from the undrifted fr.pos while CornerMinute films the drifted p, so a drifting card-up shot slides the face off its x. The ruler's u=0/0.5/1 all film the same lens.
problems.fix: In lens(): var p: Vector3 = (fr['pos'] as Vector3) + (fr.get('drift', Vector3.ZERO) as Vector3) * u, and return that p; in CornerMinute._camera use ls['pos'] (then apply the behind lerp to it) instead of its own p

problems.issue: Points are projected by hand instead of with the game camera.

result.summary: PR #209 (RIBHURT1, Qwen) does what the brief asks in the code, and the code is correct. InjuryRoll gets RIB_HURT_LINE 35 and HURT_WEIGHT 3, with the ribs row weighted in both loops exactly as cut is. Injuries.after_bout builds one places dict (head formula untouched, plus the five body-map places when m carries a body_map with an "a" side) and passes it to both bout_roll and bout_cause. Old saves without a body map take the head-only path as before. No file the PR touches has changed on main since the merge base c68f4493 (git log merge-base..main on all three files is empty; REST1 at 6fa2b52b did not touch them), so the diff applies cleanly. CI "tests" is red only on guard_knee_test, a known failure that has nothing to do with this PR. rib_injury_test is not in run_tests.sh, as the brief says. Three problems with the evidence. (1) Check c can only pass: it compares one seed, and both bouts are almost certainly uninjured. (2) Step 3 is half dropped: no injury chance, no cut share for the ribs case, and no injured-bouts-out-of-2,000 count before and after. (3) The PR body has no FAIL lines from main. Reading the code, checks a and d would be red on main (main ignores the ribs, so both shares and both counts come out equal, 4 vs 4), and b, c, e pass on main. Two design notes for Claude, not the seat's fault. First, m["body_map"] only exists when the bout was watched in 3D (BodyLive.attach sets modal["body_map"], scripts/fight3d/BodyLive.gd:35), so bouts settled in words or by sim never get the rib effect. Second, because bout_chance reads the worst place and the face and ribs are now in the dict, watched bouts get hurt more often overall: about 6% a bout becomes about 7.8-8.5% when a face or rib place reaches 15-35. That is the number the missing 2,000-bout measurement was meant to show.

missed: The commit message for d6579e22 says 'the face direction capture reads the head bone's basis in skeleton_updated', but tests/corner_face_scene.gd:50 stores skel.global_transform.basis * Vector3.BACK, which is the body's forward. The seat's own description of what its ruler measures is false. It is not just a known issue it owned up to.

The commit message describes the mirror check as 'the blue coach sits at the same relative position as the red coach'. That is a self-referential check, not the brief's mirror check, which runs the hand placement for red and compares it with what the real cues placed. The seat relabelled a check that can only pass as the one the brief asked for.

The game and the ruler feed different card edges into lens(). CornerMinute.gd:131 passes ui.subject_x()*2.0, which is the overlay's typed CARD_LEFT/CARD_LEFT_BODY constant (CornerOverlay.gd:244). The test passes a freshly built overlay's get_global_rect().x/1920 with no wait (corner_face_test.gd:116-128). Even a green ruler would not prove the game's framing. The brief's 'what the last round got wrong' list warns against exactly this.

The PR is a regression for the shots main already handled (side2, corner_wide, low_out with the card up). Main aimed frame_at from the drifted p. The branch aims from the undrifted fr.pos and still films p, so the face drifts off its spot during each card-up shot. The reviewer lists this under the lens/drift blocker, but it is worth calling out as a loss against main, not only a missing fix.

Mutants run once, before the per-seed state is settled, and they use face_dirs (body forward). So the mutant c lens '1 m behind the head along minus face forward' is built from the body's forward. Even with a real (c) check, it would not test the turned head.
wrong: Problem 'card_x = subject_x()*2.0 ... minor' understates the issue. Because the test passes a different card-edge value than the game, the ruler measures a lens the game never builds. That is closer to should_fix than minor.

The claim that the un-awaited _read_card 'explains the 208 vs 274 failure counts' is not proven. The crew.build() leak in apply_seed (fresh unplaced crew, extra CornerIK each seed) and the no-wait overlays in the card-state loop are equally likely causes. Treat it as one plausible cause, not the explanation.

missed: Check d's 2x does not isolate the new ribs weighting. With left_ribs 15 the ribs place is also the worst place, so bout_chance rises about 1.5x (s 0.85 vs 0.44: (0.4+1.02)/(0.4+0.53)). The expected ratio is therefore about 3.8x, and the measured 8 vs 4 (exactly 2.0) is a small, noisy sample of about 24 injuries out of 400. Only check a measures the weighting on its own. Check d stays red on main by reading (main ignores body_map, so 4 vs 4).

The test sets the ribs value by hand (bm_hurt['a']['places']['left_ribs'] = 15.0). The brief asked for BodyMap's own functions if one exists. BodyMap.add_beats with landed body_hook beats would do it, although it needs many beats. Acceptable, but the brief's wording was not followed to the letter.

Check c also passes on main and against any mutant of the body-map branch that does not crash. With a fresh map, every added place is 100 and the head (56) stays the worst, so the roll is identical by construction, whatever the seed. It can never be red.
wrong: Problem 3 (check d does not use Data.lucy) is mostly made up. Career.quick_start starts with an empty fighters list and sets c.applicant = ClubStart.walkin(c.start, Data.lucy()). Sim.sign then signs that applicant and Roster appends it, so c.fighter() after Sim.sign IS the quick-start Lucy, as the brief asked. Only the c.cash = 1000000 line is unneeded.

Problem 5's framing is off. On main, bout_cause only ever received {head}, so a rib injury already read 'from the head shots taken'. The PR does not make the reason stop following the damage, because it never did. With ribs now the worst place, a rib injury reads 'from the rounds boxed', which is slightly better. The follow-up (name the body or face shots) is still worth doing.

The drift estimate 'about 7.8-8.5%' is slightly narrow. A worst face or rib place at 35 gives 0.06 x (0.4 + 1.2 x 0.65) = about 7.1%, and at 15 about 8.5%, so the range is about 7.1-8.5%. This is minor and does not change the verdict.

result.summary:
PR #210 (HUMANFIGHT2B) should be rejected. Nothing goes onto main. It reports HUMAN_MOTION_TEST failures=0, but that green is false. I re-read the seat's own two arms with Python (read-only). The arms are in %APPDATA%/Godot/app_userdata/FightCamp/hm2_on and hm2_off, written at 19:19 by the PR's own run. Five findings:

(1) ReachBand gives a clip with no measured reach a perfect score (miss 0). So the ON arm stops playing the Punch PRO and captured takes. Every punch falls back to the old generic clips 'jab', 'cross', 'lead_hook' and 'body_hook'. Every punch's hand column is empty and its contact time is the 0.267 s default. One rear_hook is thrown as a lead_hook, the other hand (beat at t=12.067). The OFF arm plays pro_left_jab_c, pro_right_cross_b, pro_right_hook and so on.

(2) The before/after taps ran on only 9 of 2700 rows (tap_ok). So B2, B3 and B4 skip almost every frame and pass without testing anything. The arm-pop bar only counts a turn the taps confirm, so it is silenced too. The shown pose in the ON arm still has 3 arm or trunk turns over 25 degrees at clip starts: boxer 0 frame 591 at 44 degrees; boxer 1 frames 253 and 370. The ruler printed none of them as FAIL.

(3) The contact bar does not count a landed punch that never touches. With the hand column empty, the ruler measures the right glove on every punch. Result: touched=0, a pass that proves nothing. Read correctly, only 1 of 9 landed punches touches in the ON arm, against 3 of 9 in the OFF arm (today's main).

(4) PostureLimit sits after FootLock and FloorStand, against the brief. The ruler's taps do not bracket it, so B2, B3 and B4 never see it. It also rotates the foot bone, found through the bone tree, so the B3a name scan never catches it.

(5) Four regression tests went red: human_feet 1, boxer_footwork 2, head_aim 12 (0 on recent PRs) and block_meet 7 (1 on main).

Nothing visual was delivered: no result page, no BEFORE numbers, no film, no sheets, no stills. Other missing items: the ruler was not committed alone first, and the four GUARD_KNEE numbers are not quoted.

Merge-base check: no file this PR changes has changed on main since its merge base (3b4b1daf). REST1 (6fa2b52b) is already in the base and touches none of these files. So the diff would apply cleanly today; it is the content that is wrong.

The next round can start from this branch's ruler files (tests/human_motion_lib.gd, tests/human_motion_test.gd, tools/human_fight_tap.gd, the film columns and BeatFire's public log), once the fixes below are made.

But :131-157 counts a hip or arm pop only when the post tap also shows it ('own'). Taps ran on only 9 of 2700 ON rows, so the arm-start bar is effectively off. problems.issue: A clip with no measured reach returns miss 0.0, which scores best. Every beat in the ON arm becomes the generic fallback clip (jab, cross, lead_hook, body_hook) instead of the Punch PRO or captured takes. The rear_hook plays lead_hook, the other hand. Contact rows and hands are lost (BeatFire hand=''), and FightStage.land arms lead_hook on the RIGHT hand.
problems.fix: In _miss/_score, treat an unmeasured clip as not a candidate (score INF) and never let choose() return a clip with no reach. Limit candidates to the takes of the move's own stem (names that start with 'pro_'+PUNCH[move][0] or the move's rk take). Drop PUNCH[move][2] and other-hand fallbacks. If no take is measured, return BeatClips' own pick unchanged. Add a ruler check that every logged clip's hand and stem match the move.

problems.issue: Tap frames are compared with Engine.get_process_frames() just after 'await process_frame', before the skeleton updates that frame. tap_ok=1 on only 9 of 2700 rows, so B2, B3 and B4 skip almost everything and the arm-pop 'own' filter switches the arm bar off.
problems.fix: In _store_pose (the skeleton_updated handler), record bx['hf_frame']=Engine.get_process_frames() and copy both taps' pose dicts there. In _tail, set tap_ok when both taps' frame equals hf_frame. In human_motion_lib.gd, add FAIL when the ON arm's tap_ok share is under 90% of rows (the ruler is blind).

problems.issue: Pops count only when the post tap also shows the pop. Arm-start turns caused by later layers (or seen while the taps were off) go to later_arm with no FAIL. The ON arm has 3 shown turns over 25 degrees at clip starts that read green.
problems.fix: Score arm_start on the SHOWN rotations (cur/prev _q) with no 'own' filter. Keep the tap split only for hips, as the brief allows ('if the hip pops left come from a feet layer, show it with the numbers'), and print later_hip beside it.

problems.issue: A landed, not-cut punch with no touch frame (no_touch) is not a failure, and an empty hand silently becomes Rface (:195). With touched=0 the contact bar can only pass.
problems.fix: Count no_touch as bad_len (FAIL contact). FAIL when a landed beat's 'hand' is empty. Take the hand from the clip's own row, or from the move's lead/rear side, never a default.

problems.issue: PostureLimit is moved after FootLock and FloorStand, which the brief bans ('the feet layers keep the last word ... never cap after the feet layers'). It sits outside the taps, so B2, B3 and B4 never see it.
problems.fix: Leave PostureLimit out of this merge. In the next round, place it next to PopCap before the first feet layer, add 'PostureLimit' to human_fight_film.gd NEW_MODS, and if the knee bar cannot pass there, report the numbers instead of moving the clamp after the feet.

problems.issue: Writes the ankle (Foot) bone's rotation through a bone found by hierarchy (_chain), so B3(a)'s source scan for 'Foot' cannot see that a new module drives a foot bone.
problems.fix: No foot-bone write in any new module. Turn only the UpperLeg (and LowerLeg if needed) and let the feet layers own the foot. Extend B3a to flag set_bone_* calls on any index that _chain resolves past LowerLeg, or check B3b with working taps.

problems.issue: Hips is capped LAST with set_bone_global_pose. Turning the hips afterwards re-rotates the spine, arms and head that were already capped, so the per-bone cap no longer holds on what is shown, and the hip-origin write moves the feet (B3b).
problems.fix: Order BONES parent first (Hips, Spine, Chest, Neck, Head, shoulders, upper arms, lower arms, hands) and read each child's global pose after its parent was written. Note in the result page that the hip-origin cap moves the feet, and measure B3b with working taps.

problems.issue: B5(a) accepts the logged clip anywhere from t-0.08 to t+0.12 s, including frames BEFORE the punch, so a repeated clip (jab after jab) passes even if the new one never started.
problems.fix: Look only at the first frame with row t >= entry t for the hitter, and require clip == logged clip or play_id > punch_id there.

problems.issue: REACH_CHECK=false and posture REPORT while ReachBand and PostureLimit ship ON (meta reach=1, posture=1). The brief says a part's bar becomes a check in the same commit the part ships.
problems.fix: Either ship the part OFF (REPORT stays) or set REACH_CHECK=true and make the posture knee/lean bars FAIL in the same commit.

problems.issue: set_hold(1/30, 1/30) drops PunchReach's correction from full to zero in one frame. If the correction is large, the glove snaps home: a visible pop no ruler or film checks.
problems.fix: Keep the 1-frame hold but give the out ease 3-4 frames (0.10-0.13 s), and add a ruler check on the glove's per-frame step in the 3 frames after contact.

problems.issue: Missing: BEFORE/AFTER table, FAIL lines on main, stack order, the four GUARD_KNEE numbers, 60 s film (mp4), four numbered sheets. VISUAL PR with nothing to look at.
problems.fix: Next round: commit the fixed ruler alone with BEFORE numbers on main first, then the fixes, the film on the hidden desktop and the four sheets named in the brief.

problems.issue: Regressions on the branch: head_aim 12 failures (0 on PR 202), human_feet 1, boxer_footwork 2, block_meet 7 (main 1). Most likely from the fallback-clip swap (no contact rows) and PostureLimit after the feet layers.
problems.fix: After the ReachBand and PostureLimit fixes, re-run these four on the branch and on main side by side, and quote both counts in the PR.

missed: tests/human_motion_test.gd _arm() never clears user://hm2_on / hm2_off before the child run and ignores a non-zero child exit code: it only prints the log tail and adds no FAIL. If the child crashes or stops early, Lib.judge reads stale shown.csv/beats.csv from an earlier run, so the test can pass without filming anything. The fix: delete the arm's csv files first and count child exit != 0 (or a missing or short shown.csv) as a FAIL.

The contact and B-ban bars are judged only on the ON arm (judge() calls _contact, _b1, _b2b3b4 and _b5 with on_* only). The OFF arm, which is today's main, never gets a contact or ban reading. So the brief's step 2 rule ("run the ruler on today's main, quote the FAIL lines; a bar green where the critics saw the fault means the ruler is wrong") cannot be met by this ruler even after a rerun. Recomputed: the OFF arm touches only 3 of 9 landed punches, yet it would print no contact FAIL either, because no_touch is not a failure.

ReachBand mixes two kinds of number. For Punch PRO clips, _reach returns clip_contact.json reach_m (a positive reach, 0.17-0.30 m). For rk takes, it returns the warm() cache gap_m - (p.z*sc + 0.10), which is a remaining distance. _miss adds either one to (gap - gap_m) the same way, so its 'miss' has no single meaning. The 0.28 wants_step threshold is also hand-typed. Beyond the miss=0 bug, the band logic is not grounded in measured reach.

BeatFire's step_first path (ReachBand.wants_step) calls stage.step(who, 1) and pushes the beat at least 0.40 s later (base = maxf(base, t + 0.40)). No ruler bar measures this new beat delay or the step it adds. A delayed beat also moves the sound and hit timing with it.

block_meet going from 1 to 7 failures is more likely from ContactBeat.tune being added to FightStage.arm_block (hold 1/30, out 1/30 on BLOCKED punches, so the glove leaves the blocking glove after one frame) than from the reviewer's guesses (the fallback-clip swap and PostureLimit). The next brief should name arm_block's ContactBeat.tune as a suspect.
BeatFire.gd adds a member named 'log', which shadows GDScript's built-in log() function (a shadowing warning). It is not fatal, but it is a GDScript trap; a name like beat_log is safer.

The child film's fight clock reads 'fight t 34.93' over 1350 frames (arm.log). The secs=45 window holds about 35 s of fight, under the brief's 'at least 40 s' of bout, so the 1b film-length check the reviewer marked as met is short.
